bug_semantics: Alist's DefaultConfig() set TlsInsecureSkipVerify to true, so first-run config.json and any upgrade whose config.json lacked that key inherited skip-verify. Shared outbound HTTP clients (drivers/base RestyClient/NoRedirectClient and later InitClient/NewHttpClient) built tls.Config{InsecureSkipVerify: conf.Conf.TlsInsecureSkipVerify}, so storage-driver TLS accepted attacker certificates. A network MitM (DNS hijack, rogue AP, ARP spoof) can decrypt/steal/tamper storage credentials and file traffic. CVE-2026-25160 / GHSA-8jmm-3xwx-w974 (CWE-295); official range < 3.57.0, patched in 3.57.0. Code shows the insecure default from the v3.12.0 tag through v3.56.0 (v3.11.0 still defaulted false).
flaw_origin: The skip-verify flag itself was added securely: 7bc46de8aabc5d40d7fae04689725201685d4241 (2023-02-08, BoYanZh) introduced TlsInsecureSkipVerify with DefaultConfig false and only applied InsecureSkipVerify when the flag was true. The vulnerability is the later default flip: c8f3e8ab4d2fc8359266399484f863f3515dddfa (2023-02-23, Andy Hsu) is a one-line, single-parent commit 'feat!: skip tls insecure verify by default' changing TlsInsecureSkipVerify: false to true in internal/conf/config.go. Immediate parent 4be8524d8071890df6f32f1396bc61122defb71f still has false and the parent tree has no TlsInsecureSkipVerify: true. That first-write survived (git blame at v3.56.0 and at the fix first-parent still attributes the true default to c8f3e8ab). Later a3446720a265ad43cce2efb9a30487eadd21e65e only broadened where the already-true flag was applied. The 2026 fix restored the secure default.

reasoning: Vulnerability-first: CVE-2026-25160 is a published (not withdrawn/rejected) CWE-295 finding that Alist skipped TLS certificate verification by default on outbound storage-driver HTTP. The cited sink is DefaultConfig()'s TlsInsecureSkipVerify: true, which InitConfig uses as the base struct (so new installs and configs missing the JSON key get skip-verify) and which shared clients copy into crypto/tls.Config.InsecureSkipVerify. That is a real MitM of storage credentials and file bytes, matching the GHSA PoC against weiyun. The smallest first-write of those vulnerable lines is c8f3e8ab4d2fc8359266399484f863f3515dddfa: it is not the 7bc46de8 flag introduction (that defaulted false and is therefore not the insecure mechanism), not a later wiring expansion (a3446720 only consumed the already-true flag), and not a move/squash/release wrapper (one parent, one-line hunk, parent tree lacks TlsInsecureSkipVerify: true). The line remains attributed to that SHA at v3.56.0 and at the fix first-parent. Version checks hold: BIC is exactly tag v3.12.0, precedes v3.56.0, and the merge fix 69629ca / member 66a52b8 is an ancestor of v3.57.0 where the default is false. AI second, BIC-only: the introducer commit object is human maintainer Andy Hsu <i@nn.ci> as both author and committer with no AI/co-author/bot trailers, so the verdict is NOT_AI.
